newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian tells of father's ordeal in Red Terror.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian tells of father's ordeal in Red Terror.

text.p: A prosecution witness told an Ethiopian court on Tuesday how his father, left for dead in the 1970s Red Terror campaign against Marxist opponents, managed to return home badly wounded -- only to be "finished off" later.
The witness was testifying at the trial of 71 former officials of Ethiopia's military junta known as the Dergue, which was toppled in 1991.

"It was one evening in 1978. My mother, sisters and myself were sitting huddled together after we learned that our father was taken by revolutionary guards," said the witness, who was only nine years old at the time.
"We heard a knock and opened the door. To our surprise, it was our father soaked with blood and gasping for air.
"He kissed all of us and told us that he was mortally wounded by the chairman of District 9, Kelbesa Negewo and his secretary Senaite," said the witness.
But the guards who had left him for dead on a roadside discovered the body was missing, and "came home, took him and finished him off," he added.
Kelbesa and Senaite are charged with murder during the Red Terror campaign of 1977/78, launched by Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam to eliminate opponents.

They are accused of genocide and crimes against humanity and face the death penalty if found guilty. Only 46 of the 71 accused Dergue officials are in court. The remaining 25, including Mengistu who lives in exile in Zimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
Ethiopian prosecutors have charged a total of 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide under the Dergue.
